title: Shutdown and Trade Risk
brief: Which players could be shut down late in the season or traded before the deadline, and how does that affect their value for our March 28 end? It must flag who matters most for playoff weeks 19 to 21 and which young players could gain if a veteran is moved.
summary: Our season ends on 2027-03-28, so March rest hurts us in the weeks that decide the title. Shutdown risk sits mostly with teams that have no reason to win or lose in March, such as Brooklyn, Milwaukee, the Clippers, New Orleans and Dallas, plus teams that may rest veterans. Pay the low end of a player's range when his March minutes are uncertain, sell those players before the 2027-03-04 deadline, and save FAB for young players whose roles grow after veterans are traded.

paragraphs.text: Once a team decides to tank, it may shut down injured players for the rest of the season, even players who could have returned. In our league that loss lands in weeks 19 to 21, when every game counts.

Teams that do not control their own pick are a separate risk. The notes name the Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans and Mavericks. They have no reason to tank and no reason to push for wins. So they may rest players, be extra careful with injuries, or give young players minutes late in the season. Brooklyn and Milwaukee are the main examples.

A team with nothing to play for in March can cut its veterans' minutes to develop young players. The same goes for stars on bad teams. Value them on a range that includes rest and fewer minutes, not just on per-game value. In practice, bid near the bottom of their fair price range, not the top.

Julius Randle matters most here. Brooklyn may rest him in March so young players get time, and that cuts straight into our playoff weeks. Draft him only inside his fair range, and plan to trade him before the 2027-03-04 deadline. After that date you cannot move him in our league.

Michael Porter Jr. and Moritz Wagner are also on Brooklyn, and their March minutes are uncertain. Porter is still worth drafting, but keep your bid in the lower part of his range. Wagner is a waiver name only.

Darius Garland carries only a small risk of late-season rest on the Clippers. That small risk does not change his fair price, but check his minutes in February before you decide whether to hold him for the playoffs. Golden State may rest Draymond Green and Al Horford for lottery odds. Both are fringe players, so the risk only matters if you pick them up. Sacramento could pull Zach LaVine's minutes or bench him as it builds for the future.

Dallas is a no-pick team with a playoff schedule of 4, 4 and 4 games. Kyrie Irving could get only 10 of those games if he keeps resting on back-to-backs. Milwaukee is a no-pick team too, so watch the minutes of Ryan Rollins and Tyler Herro in February.

sections.heading: Trade risk: when a move cuts value

paragraphs.text: Projections assume trade candidates stay all season, so they do not price in a role change. For some players a trade is the main downside. A trade to a good team could cut Domantas Sabonis's role. A deal could lower Porter's usage further and shrink Cameron Johnson's role. A move into a third-option role would sink Norman Powell's value. Do not pay extra for these players because of trade hopes.

Several early-round guards also carry trade tags: Jamal Murray (salary), Austin Reaves (if the Lakers struggle) and Trey Murphy III (high asking price). The notes do not say a trade would hurt their stats. So pay their normal prices, and check trade news each week from January until 2027-03-04.

Rudy Gobert could be traded if Minnesota's season goes badly. Minnesota also plays only two games in our week 20, so a punt FT team should plan a streaming spot for that week. Mark Williams is expected back only in mid to late March and may be traded at the deadline. At best he is a short playoff pickup.

The experts split on two veterans. On Kyrie Irving, several experts say a trade is possible, but one heard no trade talk. On Jrue Holiday, one expert said in June that he will likely be moved, but a later team preview doubts a consolidation trade. Anthony Davis is expected to stay in Washington, but the Golden State rumors leave a deadline move possible. For all three, draft on current role and price, and do not pay for a trade that may not come.

Because projections assume veterans stay, they can understate the young players behind them. The clearest case is Orlando. It is near the second apron and likely has to choose between Jalen Suggs and Anthony Black. A Suggs trade or injury is what would make Black startable.

Other waiver names to track: Scoot Henderson is named as a likely outgoing piece in a rumored Jaylen Brown trade. Malik Monk could be traded into a bigger role. Burries is Milwaukee's long-term shooting guard behind Herro. Kasparas Jakučionis needs real minutes in that crowded backcourt or a trade. In Chicago, Jalen Smith's role is tied to Leonard Miller. Add Smith at once if he starts.

Plan for it. Keep part of your FAB for the days around 2027-03-04, and keep one roster spot open for a moved or promoted player. We get only 6 acquisitions per week. In weeks 19 to 21, spend them on players who are sure to play.

players.line: Davis is elite per game, and his risk is games played plus Golden State rumors; the experts expect him to stay.
Murray could be traded to shed salary, but no note says a move would cut his all-category line.
Reaves could be moved only if the Lakers struggle, so check the standings and news before the deadline.
Murphy plays for a no-pick New Orleans team and has a high trade price, so watch both his March minutes and trade news.
A trade to a good team could cut Sabonis's role, so do not pay extra on trade hopes.
Kyrie is on a no-pick Dallas team and rests on back-to-backs, which could leave him only 10 playoff games, and experts split on a trade.
Garland carries a small late-rest risk on a Clippers team with no strong reason to win or lose.
Porter has uncertain March minutes in Brooklyn, and a trade could cut his usage, so keep bids in the lower half of his range.
Brooklyn may rest Randle in March for young players, so plan to trade him before 2027-03-04.
Rollins is on a no-pick Milwaukee team and is cheap enough that Milwaukee could trade him for picks.
Herro is on an expiring deal with Burries as the long-term shooting guard, so a deadline move is possible.
Gobert could be traded if Minnesota struggles, and his two-game week 20 needs a streaming plan.
Chicago signs veterans to flip them, and a move into a third-option role would sink Powell's value.
Orlando may trade Suggs to keep Black under the second apron, which adds to his games-played risk.
LaVine faces both trade and shutdown risk on a rebuilding Sacramento team that could bench him or buy him out.
Dallas has shopped Gafford, so his early starting role may not last.
Barrett becomes a deadline trade candidate if Toronto starts badly.
Gordon is a possible Denver trade piece with limited availability, so he is only a bench bid or a streamer.
Experts disagree on whether Holiday is moved, and his value only rises when Portland's guards miss games.
Johnson is expected to be traded so Denver can get under the second apron, and a deal could shrink his role.
Golden State may rest veterans for lottery odds, which threatens Green's March games.
Jaquez is seen as a likely trade piece, possibly to Denver, so his role depends on where he lands.
Grant is a possible Memphis deadline chip, so check his minutes and trade news.
Braun is named with Cam Johnson as a possible Denver trade piece, and the experts call him overvalued.
A Suggs trade or injury is what would make Black startable.
A rumored Jaylen Brown trade could send Henderson to a new team with more minutes.
Monk has continuing trade rumors and could be moved into a bigger role.
Smith's role is tied to Leonard Miller and Claxton, so add him at once if he starts.
Williams returns only around mid to late March and may be traded at the deadline, so he is a short playoff pickup at best.
Jakučionis is valued as a trade chip and needs a trade or real minutes in Milwaukee's crowded backcourt.
McBride has no extension and is a trade candidate, so a move could change his bench role.
Green does not fit Milwaukee's new direction, and a trade could open threes-only streaming value.
Dort could be traded again if Daniels makes him expendable, and he is a deep-league option only.
Golden State may rest Horford, and he already skips back-to-backs, so he is a short-term waiver option at most.
Gueye is a possible piece in a small roster-cutting trade and matters only if injuries open minutes.
Brooklyn may move March minutes to young players, which works against Wagner in our playoffs.
